final:
I added both methods to `Ledger` in `ledger/entries.py`. The existing tests pass (4 passed), and a quick manual check returned entries oldest first. I didn't add new test cases.

- **`post_end_of_day(account, amount, day)`**: posts the entry at 23:59:59 on `day`, in UTC. The `Entry` rule says `posted_at` is always timezone-aware UTC, so I treated `day` as a UTC calendar day. It goes through the existing `post`.
- **`entries_since(since)`**: returns entries with `posted_at >= since`, sorted oldest first. Entries can be posted with any explicit timestamp, so the list isn't necessarily in time order, and the method sorts to be sure.

`entries_since` raises `ValueError` if `since` is naive. Comparing a naive datetime to the aware `posted_at` values would otherwise fail with a less clear `TypeError`. An aware `since` in any timezone works.

I didn't change any rules, so no `# Rule:` comments were touched.
